first_impression.reaction: Googled 'santorini or mykonos wedding' expecting a listicle that crowns one island and sells me a package. Instead the intro says 'a choice between two settings, not two standards' and the short answer is 'Neither island wins.' Fine, at least nobody's pretending. I jumped to the FAQ, then the comparison table, then read the season, travel and legal sections properly. Named sources, dated Smartraveller advice, and an admission that neither island has its own weather station. That's the stuff I trust. A few lines go further than the page's own facts, mainly on chapels, and the cost FAQ leans on an opinion it can't show me.

journey.section: Santorini or Mykonos for your wedding: the short answer
journey.quote: Neither island wins. They answer different questions.
journey.reaction: Good. No fake 'number one'. I'd have assumed a winner meant someone got paid to say it.

journey.section: Santorini vs Mykonos at a glance
journey.quote: The same seven questions, answered for each island. This is a comparison, not a ranking.
journey.reaction: Same rows for both. Easy to scan, easy to drop into my spreadsheet.

journey.section: Santorini vs Mykonos at a glance
journey.quote: If you already know your dates, guest count and ceremony type, [book a Wedded Concierge consultation](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=santorini-or-mykonos-wedding&utm_content=primary) and test both islands against them.
journey.reaction: Pitch straight after the table, before a single venue is described. Not pushy, but proof first, then ask.

Says who? More than what? The page lists chapels at four Mykonos hotels and none at the six Santorini ones, so maybe it means 'among these venues'. As written it's a claim about the whole island with nothing behind it.

journey.quote: Mykonos Grand states that both partners must be Christian Orthodox for a religious wedding on the hotel premises.
journey.reaction: This is the catch I'm always looking for, and they put it on the page. Useful, and it makes the rest more believable.

journey.quote: The beaches are unlike anything at home, with black, red and white sand and multicoloured pebbles below steep cliffs.
journey.reaction: 'Unlike anything at home' is brochure talk. The colours are a fact; the rest is a vibe. Minor.

journey.quote: The venues reflect a broad guest list. The Myconian Collection has certified halal and kosher kitchens and a South Asian chef for traditional Indian cuisine.
journey.reaction: Good detail, but it's one hotel group. 'The venues' makes it sound island-wide.

journey.quote: In most cases passengers carry their own luggage up and down stairs, and some services lack suitable access for people with disabilities.
journey.reaction: My parents would be on that ferry. Nobody else tells you this. Dated to Smartraveller, too.

journey.section: When to marry on each island
journey.quote: The [Hellenic National Meteorological Service](https://www.hnms.gr/) has no climate station on Santorini or Mykonos; for the South Aegean it lists only Naxos and Rodos.
journey.reaction: Admits the data limit and uses the nearest station, labelled as such. That's exactly how I'd want it done.

journey.section: When to marry on each island
journey.quote: Smartraveller also notes that Greece sits in an active seismic zone, with earthquakes and volcanic activity near major destinations including Santorini, and advises following local authorities.
journey.reaction: They mention the volcano risk on the island they'd be selling me. Honest about trade-offs.

journey.section: Getting legally married on either island, in brief
journey.quote: An appointment is needed for all notarial services, and a fee applies.
journey.reaction: Concrete and checkable. Paired with 'the embassy does not give legal advice', it doesn't pretend everything is handled for me.

journey.quote: **You want a chapel above a beach.** Mykonos. Santa Marina, Mykonos Grand, Saint John and the Myconian Collection all have whitewashed chapels by the water.
journey.reaction: Earlier the page only says vows can be taken at Agia Fotini Chapel at Saint John, nothing about it being whitewashed or by the water. And the Myconian chapel is just 'small whitewashed', no location. The summary is tidier than the facts.

journey.section: Santorini or Mykonos wedding questions, answered
journey.quote: The island matters less than the choices you make on it.
journey.reaction: I get that there are no prices, and the list of cost drivers is fair. But this opening line is an opinion stated as fact, with nothing on the page to back it. Say what drives cost and stop there.

journey.section: Choose your island with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: The fee is agreed in writing before any work begins, and inclusions are confirmed in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Right signal. Still doesn't tell me whether venues pay you too, but that's a question for a call.

unanswered_questions: Is 'Mykonos has more chapels' about the island as a whole or only the venues listed here?
Is Saint John's Agia Fotini Chapel actually whitewashed and by the water, as the scenario section implies?
Does Wedded Wonderland take a commission or mark-up from any of these venues? (deferred business detail)
Is there a real Santorini or Mykonos wedding with the actual budget I can look at?

turn_offs_found.why: It's a comparison stated as fact with no number or source. The page's own venue list half-supports it, but the sentence claims the whole island. Once I catch one of these I start checking everything else.

turn_offs_found.quote: **You want a chapel above a beach.** Mykonos. Santa Marina, Mykonos Grand, Saint John and the Myconian Collection all have whitewashed chapels by the water.
turn_offs_found.why: The venue sections don't say Saint John's chapel is whitewashed or by the water, or where the Myconian chapel sits. The summary rounds the facts up, which is exactly what marketing does.

turn_offs_found.quote: The island matters less than the choices you make on it.
turn_offs_found.why: An unsupported opinion at the top of the one FAQ I care most about. The cost drivers that follow are fine; the opener reads like a way of dodging the question.

turn_offs_found.quote: If you already know your dates, guest count and ceremony type, [book a Wedded Concierge consultation](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=santorini-or-mykonos-wedding&utm_content=primary) and test both islands against them.
turn_offs_found.why: A CTA before any venue is described. Soft wording, so minor, but the evidence should come before the ask.

turn_offs_found.quote: The beaches are unlike anything at home, with black, red and white sand and multicoloured pebbles below steep cliffs.
turn_offs_found.why: Emotional filler on top of a fact. Doesn't hurt much, but it's the tone I tune out.

would_share_with: My fiancee, the at-a-glance table and the 'Which island suits you' scenarios
My parents, the ferry access paragraph and the heat, wildfire and seismic notes

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [start planning with Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=santorini-or-mykonos-wedding&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: Mostly earned. No winner forced on me, dated sources, real catches (the Orthodox rule, ferry stairs, no local weather station) and 'in writing' on the fee. What holds me back is a couple of lines that go further than the facts, especially on chapels, and I'd still want to know whether you take a cut from venues.

top_3_changes: Must-fix: support or scope 'Mykonos has more chapels.' (Ceremony types, On Mykonos). For example, 'More of the Mykonos venues here have their own chapel.' That keeps it to what the venue list shows.

Must-fix: align the scenario line 'Santa Marina, Mykonos Grand, Saint John and the Myconian Collection all have whitewashed chapels by the water.' with the venue facts. Saint John's Agia Fotini Chapel isn't described as whitewashed or by the water, and the Myconian chapel's location isn't stated. Either drop the venues the facts don't cover or reword it to 'have their own chapels'.

Tighten the unsupported opinions. Cut or soften 'The island matters less than the choices you make on it.' in the cost FAQ and lead with the cost drivers. Change 'The venues reflect a broad guest list' to name the Myconian Collection. Optional: trim 'unlike anything at home' and move the primary CTA below the venue sections so the evidence comes before the ask.
